title: Transformers & LLM Internals
blurb: How a modern large language model is built, from self-attention up to model anatomy. The architecture that won, and what's actually inside the boxes labeled 'LLM' in every system diagram.

nodes.label: Self-attention
nodes.description: Query / key / value, scaled dot-product, the softmax, what attention 'looks at'. The single most-important operation in modern AI.
nodes.doneWhen: You can derive scaled dot-product attention from first principles and explain the role of each Q/K/V.

nodes.label: Multi-head attention
nodes.description: Why multiple heads, what they specialize on, how heads are concatenated and projected. The 'multi-head' that makes the architecture flexible.
nodes.doneWhen: You can implement multi-head attention from scratch in PyTorch.

nodes.label: The Transformer architecture
nodes.description: Encoder / decoder / decoder-only. The block: attention + feed-forward + residual + norm. How modern LLMs are stacks of identical blocks.
nodes.doneWhen: You can sketch a decoder-only transformer's forward pass on a whiteboard and explain the residual stream.

nodes.label: Tokenization (BPE, SentencePiece)
nodes.description: Why we tokenize subwords, how BPE works, how vocabularies are chosen, why tokenization shapes everything downstream (cost, multilinguality, edge-case behavior).
nodes.doneWhen: You can explain why a string-length and a token-length differ, and predict tokenization weirdness for code or non-English text.

nodes.label: Positional encoding & RoPE
nodes.description: Sinusoidal vs learned vs RoPE vs ALiBi. Why position matters, and why the rotary embedding family won the modern LLM.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe what RoPE does and why it generalizes better to long contexts than absolute positions.

nodes.label: Pretraining objectives
nodes.description: Next-token prediction (causal LM), masked LM, prefix-LM, span corruption. Why next-token won, and what it means for what an LLM can do.
nodes.doneWhen: You can explain why next-token-prediction trains a surprisingly capable model.

nodes.label: Scaling laws & compute economics
nodes.description: Kaplan / Chinchilla / DeepMind scaling laws, parameter count vs data vs compute, the empirical curves. The reason the field moves the way it moves.
nodes.doneWhen: You can read a scaling-law plot and explain what it tells you about training budget.

nodes.label: Anatomy of a 2026 LLM
nodes.description: What's actually inside a modern frontier model: decoder-only stack, GQA, SwiGLU, RoPE, MoE, KV cache, long-context techniques. The picture you should have when someone says 'an LLM'.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe the anatomy of a typical open-weights 2026 LLM and explain each design choice in one sentence.
